meta.title: Seasons Around the World — Vocabulary Set 3
meta.subject: English Vocabulary
meta.description: Vocabulary practice focusing on Week 14 words: weather, rain, dry, equator, sunlight, Antarctica, coldest, store.

questions.question: Which of these is the coldest place on Earth?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the freezing continent at the South Pole, and it is the coldest place on Earth.

questions.question: The 'equator' is the imaginary line that divides the Earth in half.
questions.explanation: True. The equator is the imaginary circle around Earth that is halfway between the North and South Poles.

questions.question: Which word refers to what it is like outside, such as sunny, rainy, or windy?
questions.explanation: Weather describes the conditions of the atmosphere, like temperature, rain, wind, or sun.

questions.question: The word 'dry' describes weather with a lot of heavy rainfall.
questions.explanation: False. 'Dry' means having no water or very little rain.

questions.question: What is the name for the light that comes directly from the sun?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is the light and warmth provided by the sun, which helps plants grow.

questions.question: Water falling in drops from the clouds is called _______.
questions.explanation: Rain is liquid water that falls from the clouds to wet the ground.

questions.question: What does the verb 'store' mean?
options: To buy things at a shop
To save or keep things for later use
To fly to Mexico in fall
questions.explanation: To 'store' means to collect and keep food or items so you can use them in the future.

questions.question: Sort these Week 14 words into Places/Lines or Weather elements:
questions.explanation: 'Equator' and 'Antarctica' are geographic places/lines. 'Rain,' 'sunlight,' and 'dry' describe weather components.

questions.question: The weather near the equator is very cold and snowy all year round.
questions.explanation: False. Near the equator, the weather is very hot and stays the same almost all year.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what sunlight does:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Sunlight helps plants grow.' Sunlight provides the energy they need.

questions.question: Which word is the superlative form of 'cold,' meaning the most cold?
questions.explanation: 'Coldest' is the superlative form, describing the place or thing with the lowest temperature.

questions.question: Squirrels collect and _______ nuts in trees for the winter.
questions.explanation: Squirrels store nuts in secret tree hollows so they have food in winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe Antarctica:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth.' It is covered in ice.

questions.question: Antarctica is the coldest place, but it gets very warm in summer when the sun never sets.
questions.explanation: False. The text says: 'Even in summer, it never gets warm here' in Antarctica.

questions.question: Why is there a 'dry season' in some parts of the world?
options: Because it rains heavily every single day.
Because there is very little or no rain for several months.
Because the sun never shines in those places.
Because the ocean waves are too loud.
questions.explanation: A dry season is a period of the year with very low rainfall. It is opposite of the rainy (wet) season.
